stories.title: I think Anthropic and OpenAI have found product-market fit
stories.blurb: Simon Willison argues that Anthropic and OpenAI have crossed the threshold from hype to genuine, sustained product-market fit. With 985 comments, this is the most debated AI business take of the week. Essential reading for anyone building on top of these platforms.

stories.title: Can we have the day off?
stories.blurb: The top HN story today tackles what happens when AI does the work but humans still need to show up for the meeting. A sharp meditation on productivity, agency, and whether 'shipping faster with AI' is really the win we think it is. Mandatory reading for anyone using Claude Code daily.

stories.title: Tech CEOs are apparently suffering from AI psychosis
stories.blurb: TechCrunch names the pattern: executives making increasingly unhinged public statements about AI replacing everything, right now. A useful reality-check article when your C-suite starts forwarding AI hype to the engineering team.

stories.title: YouTube to automatically label AI-generated videos
stories.blurb: YouTube is rolling out automatic AI-content labeling for videos, leaning on detection rather than creator self-disclosure. This is a significant platform-level shift in how synthetic media gets surfaced — watch this space for downstream policy effects.

stories.title: DuckDuckGo search saw 28% more visits after Google said people love AI mode
stories.blurb: Google's insistence that users love AI Overviews is backfiring in real-time: DDG saw a 28% traffic spike the same week. Privacy-conscious developers are clearly voting with their feet — and the anti-AI-search backlash has measurable momentum.

stories.title: What Apple and Google are doing to push notifications
stories.blurb: A deep dive into how Apple and Google intercept, batch, and process push notifications at the OS level — with real privacy implications for apps that assume delivery is end-to-end. If you develop iOS or Android apps, this is essential background knowledge.

stories.title: Incident with Pull Requests, Issues, Git Operations and API Requests
stories.blurb: GitHub had a significant outage hitting PRs, Issues, and the API — basically everything a developer touches all day. The postmortem is worth reading to understand the blast radius and what to build around for resilience.

stories.title: I'm Getting into Mesh Networks (Meshtastic, MeshCore, and Reticulum)
stories.blurb: The author of Privacy Guides explores off-grid mesh networking as a privacy infrastructure alternative. A hands-on intro to Meshtastic, MeshCore, and Reticulum — timely for anyone thinking about communication resilience outside centralized platforms.

stories.title: All of human cooking compressed into 2 megabytes
stories.blurb: Researchers claim to have distilled the core structure of human culinary knowledge into a 2MB representation. A fascinating compression/information-theory result with implications for how LLMs encode domain knowledge.

stories.title: Matrix Multiplications on GPUs Run Faster When Given "Predictable" Data (2024)
stories.blurb: A counterintuitive GPU performance result: matrix multiplications run measurably faster on structured, predictable data due to hardware-level optimizations. If you're building or fine-tuning models, understanding this could directly affect your training throughput.

stories.title: Karpathy-Inspired Claude Code Guidelines
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: octo, knowledge, karpathy, claude-code, guidelines, best-practices, llm-coding, agent-skills, simplicity
stories.blurb: Four core principles for improving Claude Code behavior, derived from Andrej Karpathy's observations on LLM coding pitfalls — explicit thinking, simplicity, surgical changes, and goal-driven execution. Ships as a Claude Code plugin or CLAUDE.md drop-in. Direct hit for Claude Code users.

stories.title: Property-Based Testing with Claude red.anthropic.com
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: claude, llm, agenticEngineering, testing, propertyBasedTesting, pbt
stories.blurb: Anthropic's own engineering blog walks through using Claude for property-based testing — a notoriously hard discipline made more accessible with LLM assistance. Directly actionable for .NET/TypeScript developers who want to level up their test suites.

stories.title: Iris Photos — A native macOS photo library
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: macos, photography, dam
stories.blurb: A brand-new native macOS photo library and DAM (Digital Asset Manager) app, not just a Photos.app wrapper. For Mac users tired of Apple's photo management or Adobe's subscription lock-in, this looks like a serious contender worth watching.

stories.title: steipete/agent-scripts: Scripts for agents, shared between my repositories.
stories.blurb: Peter Steinberger's collection of reusable scripts for AI coding agents, built to be shared across projects. A practical grab-bag of glue code for anyone running Claude Code or similar agentic workflows — fork and adapt freely.

stories.title: AddyOsmani.com - Agent Skills
stories.blurb: Addy Osmani breaks down the concept of 'agent skills' — modular capabilities you can compose for AI coding agents. Directly relevant to building effective Claude Code workflows and thinking about how to structure agent behavior.

stories.title: How to Eval AI Agents — The 2026 Guide
stories.blurb: Evaluation is the unglamorous bottleneck of agentic AI development, and this guide pulls together the 2026 state of the art. If you're building with Claude Code or any LLM pipeline, getting your evals right is the difference between shipping and guessing.

stories.title: [2605.26099] Language Models Need Sleep
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: llm, ai, transformer, sleep, cache, context
stories.blurb: A new paper argues that LLMs accumulate a kind of 'context fatigue' and benefit from periodic cache-clearing analogous to sleep consolidation in biological brains. Fascinating for AI researchers and anyone thinking about long-running agent memory management.

stories.title: The State of CSS Centering in 2026
stories.blurb: CSS-Tricks surveys the surprisingly rich 2026 landscape of centering options — Flexbox, Grid, anchor positioning, and beyond. A useful reference for any frontend developer who wants to understand why so many approaches exist and which to reach for first.

stories.title: Shortcuts Archive – MacStories
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: ios, programming, ipad, iphone
stories.blurb: MacStories' exhaustive, maintained archive of Shortcuts automations for iPhone and iPad — everything from file management to Obsidian workflows. An indispensable bookmark for Apple ecosystem power users who want to automate without writing Swift.

stories.title: FFmpeg Audio Normalization: The Complete loudnorm Guide | 32blog
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: FFmpeg, howto, audio
stories.blurb: A thorough practical guide to FFmpeg's loudnorm filter for EBU R128-compliant audio normalization — exactly what you need when mastering podcasts, videos, or any audio pipeline. The two-pass workflow explanation alone is worth the click.
